issues.legal_issue: A cheque issued towards refund of a security deposit attracts liability under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act only to the extent that the cheque amount represents a legally enforceable debt when the cheque is presented.
A landlord may deduct rent and maintenance charges due for a tenant’s continued occupation from the security deposit before becoming liable to refund the balance.
Compensation for dishonoured cheques must be limited to the legally enforceable amount established by the evidence, rather than the full face value of the cheques.
